title: Duelcast onboarding eval - dual-model comparison and decision note
summary: Pairwise evaluation of two candidate model variants using the Duelcast protocol across four prompt cohorts. Recommendation: hybrid routing (short/low-cost -> Candidate A, long/knowledge -> Candidate B) with a canary rollout and targeted monitoring for factuality and latency regressions.
body:
Purpose:
This note summarizes the Duelcast-style onboarding evaluation comparing two candidate model variants for general-purpose hosted inference: Candidate A (inkbird-13b-v0.9, FP16+KV cache optimized) and Candidate B (redwood-slim-13b-v1, Q4_0 quant). Goal is to surface tradeoffs across quality, latency, and cost and produce a clear operational recommendation for model routing and rollout.

High-level takeaway:
- No single candidate dominates across all workloads.
- Candidate A has higher win-rate on short conversational and instruction prompts and is ~18% cheaper per token with batching enabled.
- Candidate B is stronger on factual/knowledge retrieval prompts and long-form summarization, with fewer hallucinations on the verification slice but incurs ~22% higher p99 latency for sequence lengths > 512.
- Recommended immediate action: hybrid routing by prompt classifier (short/instruction -> A; long/knowledge -> B) + 2-week canary with targeted eval hooks.

Experimental setup (Duelcast protocol):
- Prompt cohorts: conversation-short (CS), instruction-core (IC), knowledge-retrieval (KR), long-summarization (LS).
- Test set size: 4k prompts (1k per cohort) sampled from production shadow traffic + curated challenge sets (edgecases and adversarial items).
- Metrics: pairwise human preference (A vs B), automatic acceptability (binary), factuality score (fact-checker model), ROUGE-L for summarization, latency (p50/p95/p99), cost-per-token estimate (adjusted for batching and KV reuse).
- Experiment date range: 2026-03-03 -> 2026-03-10.
- Randomization: prompt order and seed differing between runs; n=3 reruns for automatic metrics, n=1 blinded human preference pass on 500 stratified samples.

Key quantitative results (high level):
- Overall pairwise human preference (500 sampled comparisons): Candidate A 47%, Candidate B 44%, Tie 9%  (A vs B = +3 pct points for A).
- Aggregate automatic acceptability: A 92.1%, B 91.8% (delta +0.3).
- Factuality (KR cohort): A 68.4%, B 75.2% (B +6.8 absolute).
- ROUGE-L (LS cohort): A 0.42, B 0.49 (B better on long summarization).
- Latency (batch=8, seq=128): A p99=210ms, B p99=255ms. For seq=1024: A p99=460ms, B p99=560ms.
- Cost per 1k tokens (est, hosted pricing factors + batch): A $0.058, B $0.071.

Pairwise win/loss summary by cohort (human pref on 500 stratified):
- Conversation-short (CS): A 62%  | B 28%  | Tie 10%  (A strong)
- Instruction-core (IC): A 54%  | B 38%  | Tie 8%   (A moderate)
- Knowledge-retrieval (KR): A 26%  | B 68%  | Tie 6%   (B dominant)
- Long-summarization (LS): A 33%  | B 59%  | Tie 8%  (B clear)

Automated regression flags (items failing quality gates):
- Candidate A: 34 failing items (majority in KR cohort, common failure mode = confident hallucination on entity grounding).
- Candidate B: 19 failing items (isolated failure modes on instruction-following edge cases where brevity required).

Analysis and interpretation:
- Candidate A appears better tuned for short-turn instruction and conversational fluency; lower compute path + KV cache behavior yields cost and latency wins. However, it is more prone to factual errors when the prompt requires retrieval or long context chaining.
- Candidate B trades throughput for stronger factual grounding and long-form coherence — likely due to a different pretraining blend and quantization path that preserves factual tokens better for long-context attention.
- The modest overall human preference delta masks strong cohort-specific splits; routing by prompt type unlocks >7% aggregated effective quality while reaping cost savings.

Risk assessment:
- Hallucination risk: Candidate A has non-trivial hallucination counts on KR. If routed incorrectly, customer-facing applications (search answers, legal assistant) could see spikes in incorrect assertions.
- Latency regressions: Candidate B p99 for long sequences may violate latency SLOs for synchronous APIs; need to validate tail behavior under production traffic.
- Cost variability: Candidate B increases per-token cost; hybrid routing complexity must be balanced with billing transparency.

Operational recommendation (priority list):
1) Implement prompt classifier (fast heuristic + small ML model) to route: CS + IC -> Candidate A; KR + LS -> Candidate B. Keep fallback to Candidate A for quota-constrained customers.
2) Canary rollout (2% traffic) for 7 days with real-time checks: per-route quality score, hallucination detector alerts, latency p95/p99, cost delta dashboard.
3) Instrument additional eval hooks: expanded KR probes, entity-grounding checks, and long-context degradation triggers. Run nightly mini-evals and surface top-20 failing prompts to applied-ml triage channel.
4) If canary shows >3% end-user acceptance drop or >5% hallucination increase on KR vs baseline, pause and revert to Candidate A global.
5) Post-canary: consider A/B with dynamic routing thresholds and traffic-weight tuning to achieve target cost/QoE.

Implementation notes for infra and runtime teams:
- Quantization caveat: Candidate B uses Q4_0 path that requires kernel fallback on older GPUs. Ensure fallback nodes are pinned and autoscale target adjusted for longer p99 tails.
- KV cache behavior: Candidate A benefits from prefix caching; ensure cache warmup for common prompt prefixes (session-based warmup).
- Tracing: add model-name and prompt-cohort tags to per-request traces for easy slice breakdown in console.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Can we retrain a small adapter on KR edgecases to reduce A's hallucination without losing latency advantage? (Quick experiment: 50k synthetic grounding prompts).
- Is there a middle-ground quantization profile for Candidate B that regains some latency without losing factuality? Request quantization experiments from infra team.
- How does difference manifest for embeddings (we only evaluated generation)? Schedule embeddings comparison if customers plan reranking with these models.

Attachments and references:
- Full leaderboard CSV (internal link in Confluence): CONFLUENCE-ENG-ONBOARD-227/leaderboard.csv
- Human preference annotation batch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/annotation/runs/1423
- Kernel / infra notes: JIRA-ML-789

Decision (proposed):
- Approve hybrid routing as described, start canary 2026-03-22, monitoring windows and rollback defined above.
- Track runway metric: net cost per 1M tokens and aggregated acceptance rate. Evaluate after 14 days for broader rollout.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- Focus review on KR hallucination examples (sheet tab 'KR-fails') and latency p99 tails under mixed traffic (traces available in linked infra ticket).
- If you have objections to hybrid routing (complexity reasons), propose specific acceptance thresholds (cost / latency / factuality) to compare alternatives.

Author notes / scratchpad (informal):
- Observed anecdotally: Candidate A answers casual chit-chat with more persona; some annotators flagged tone drift as positive in CS cohort.
- Consider creating a short-lived safety filter for KR outputs when routed to A as a stopgap (cheap hallucination guard).

-- end of note --
